reuse.why: The API and updated consumers reuse getScheduledAmount, but its approximate calculation reimplements the existing getApproxNumberThreshold helper.

duplication.why: Expected-amount selection remains centralized, but the rounded 7.5% tolerance formula duplicates shared/rules.ts.

placement.why: Expected-amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, with API serialization and consumer data extraction remaining in their existing layers.

scope.why: The changes focus on schedule amount policy, its consumers, the API field, and relevant tests.

maintainability.why: Centralization helps, but duplicated tolerance logic and an optional string operator behind a positional boolean make consistent adoption harder to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:getScheduledAmount calculates Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) instead of calling shared/rules.ts:getApproxNumberThreshold.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduledAmount embeds getApproxNumberThreshold's calculation inside the expectedAmount expression rather than sharing the existing definition.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount replaces rangeRounding with an optional op:string parameter and adds an isapprox branch; callers continue using the helper, but existing calls can omit the newly relevant operator.
